question: Do model-local irregularity, smooth context dependence, amplitude/frequency response preferences, normalization and mixture interference explain different aspects of known-tone response?

design.phase: One seeded phase per source, shared across every frequency/amplitude and both tones; t=0 is forecast origin
design.normalization: native versus background-locked actual normalizer and matching inverse; anchor is same background for entire surface
design.local: FP64 centered parameter derivatives; chord-midpoint model curvature removes frequency-path bend; sensitivities divide actual RMS input distances/background SD
design.interaction: f(x+a+b)-f(x+a)-f(x+b)+f(x); RMS relative to each individual effect and sum; normalize mixed effect by input-distance product
design.decodability: Fixed ridge alpha=.01, full-token hidden differences versus raw-input differences, joint fixed-frequency sine/cos coefficients; leave-one-source-out, train-only scaling and mean/permuted-label controls; exploratory only
design.provenance: Real FIT sources explicitly reused from selective_replication4942000 for instrumentation; pretraining overlap unknown. No real futures loaded.

exact_findings.claim: Sampled local responses usually shrink in relative chord curvature as radius decreases; this supports smooth context-dependent response, not globally linear behavior or universal smoothness.
exact_findings.evidence_class: L1 hidden geometry and behavioral local response

exact_findings.claim: Frequency and amplitude response preferences depend on background;19.2h is not categorically absent. The M4 native response improves strongly at amplitude2, while intermediate amplitudes can be worse.
exact_findings.evidence_class: Behavioral controlled additions; reused real FIT instrumentation

exact_findings.claim: Locking background normalization changes signal response and can harm it; it does not remove mixture interaction. Hidden and forecast interactions are distinct.
exact_findings.evidence_class: Within-model normalizer control and descriptive four-point effects

exact_findings.claim: Fourier coefficients are much easier for this fixed linear decoder to recover from locked first-block effects than native effects, but raw input is much better than either. This is neither absent-information evidence nor training attribution.
Substantial finite-radius forecast curvature remains in some contexts, especially high amplitudes. Small parameter changes are not uniformly tiny in input distance.

controls.known_signal_reference: NMSE1 is zero incremental response; true futures of real sources were never loaded.
controls.input_distance: Every local/adjacent difference records actual RMS history distance divided by background SD.
controls.curvature: Independent chord midpoint removes input frequency-path acceleration; exact FP32 midpoint rounding retained.
controls.interaction: Four-point residual divided by each marginal effect and by their sum; raw effect RMS and input-distance products saved.
controls.decoding: Leave whole source out; train-only scaling; fixed alpha=.01; raw input, training mean and shuffled-label controls;120 rows from8 source groups.

limitations: One phase per background confounds phase with context; no phase-generalization claim. Locked normalization is a counterfactual control, potentially off native manifold at high amplitude. Hidden curvature is not causal semantics.
Descriptive source-grouped summaries only; 4 synthetic seed groups and1 real FIT source per domain. No population, confirmation or general interpretability verdict.

The two narrow frequency windows do not cover the gap between24h and19.2h. Largest smallest-step input radius is about0.157 background SD; this is a finite-radius pilot, not an infinitesimal smoothness proof.
The fixed8-source interaction medians are descriptive panel summaries, not pooled-domain generalization; per-source values are preserved.
One phase per source confounds phase and context. Add a crossed phase design before attributing differences uniquely to background.
No random-initialization decoder or native-normalization-metadata-augmented decoder was run. Locked improvements must not be interpreted as learned information absent in native hidden states.
No phase-held-out or fresh-source confirmation; no causal claim about pretrained training priors.

Synthetic injection phase equals the existing5.35-cycle component phase because both use the first uniform draw from the same source seed. Near24h additions are consequently approximately phase-aligned with that background tone. This further limits any attribution of the24h-versus19.2h contrast to an intrinsic model frequency prior; use independent crossed phases and pure-tone/background controls in expansion.
instrumentation_notes: All native workers and analysis/audit completed on first attempt. Matplotlib used a temporary cache because the default config directory was read-only; plotted artifacts were written successfully.

next_decision.state: Stop; native slot2 released, no expansion launched.
next_decision.priority: First shrink actual input radii at worst-response boundaries, cross phase with context, and test native normalizer metadata in the decoder.
suggested_informative_expansions: Break synthetic phase alignment explicitly: cross independent injection phases with the same frozen backgrounds; include pure-tone and matched near/far background frequencies before labeling frequency differences intrinsic priors.
Use fixed measured RMS radii .002/.005/.01 across amplitudes and half-step convergence at the recorded worst cases, retaining chord-midpoint and FP32-floor controls.
Cross a common phase grid with each background and fresh sources; interpolate nearby backgrounds at fixed tone to directly test smooth context dependence.
Augment native hidden decoding with actual normalizer location/scale; compare raw-input and random-initialization baselines to distinguish scale accessibility from learned semantics.
Cross the same phase grid with all backgrounds, then add fresh sources; current phase and context are confounded.
Use three smaller measured input radii and half-step convergence at the worst source/cut. Compare raw path curvature with chord-corrected curvature and FP32 floors.
Bridge the24h-to19.2h frequency gap continuously, matching RMS history distances across amplitudes, with pure-tone and balanced/dominant-background controls.
Interpolate nearby backgrounds at fixed injected tone and phase to test smooth context dependence directly, then test local Jacobian transport.
Separate background-locked from locally locked normalization; test whether high-amplitude off-manifold lock artifacts explain changes.
Decode on fresh source-phase combinations against raw-input and random-initialization baselines before attributing accessibility to learned semantics.
